Speeds calibration engine

Source: R/main-calibration-engine.R
apply_gtfs_speeds_to_ssfs.Rd

Reads a reference GTFS and a target SSFS and returns that SSFS with speeds adjusted to those documented in the GTFS based on shapes and stop_times data.

Usage

apply_gtfs_speeds_to_ssfs(
  gtfs,
  ssfs,
  max_date = NULL,
  buffer_dist = 10,
  dist_factor = 0.5,
  stop_time = 10,
  osrm_speed_adj_factor = 0.72,
  accepted_route_types = c(0, 3)
)

Arguments

gtfs

An object of class 'gtfs'. Must include a shapes table.

ssfs

A ssfs list

max_date

A date within the range of gtfs$calendar$end_date representing the maximum of a 7 day range used to build the reference speed matrix from the reference GTFS. Leave as NULL to use the last 7 days of the reference GTFS

buffer_dist

A distance in meters used to define the radius of interstop speed matrix points. Defaults to 10.

dist_factor

A value between 0.1 and 0.9 used to ensure that interstops are only applied speeds from reference interstops of a similar length. Defaults to 0.5, which means that for a given interstop being calibrated, reference interstops with a distance of 50% to 150% can be used to calibrate.

stop_time

An integer in seconds, representing the amount of time added per stop made for runtimes calculated using OSRM

osrm_speed_adj_factor

A coefficient used to adjust output OSRM runtimes to make them more representative of bus runtimes.

accepted_route_types

Route types that can be used to build the reference speed matrix. By default, 0 (tramways) and 3 (buses).

Value

A ssfs list

Examples

# Calibrate Railway City Transit redesign SSFS speeds using reference GTFS
ssfs_calibrated <- apply_gtfs_speeds_to_ssfs(gtfs = gtfs_rct, ssfs = ssfs_rct2)
